operations.name: say_goodbye
operations.summary: Say that this client is leaving
operations.description: A hint, never a command. A daemon started with `--idle-exit` normally waits out its whole idle period after the last client has gone; after this request it waits only a few seconds (3), and only while nothing else happens. Running work, an open event stream, a new connection or any other request keeps it running, so another client is never cut off by one client leaving. A daemon without `--idle-exit`, such as the systemd service, ignores it. There is no request body, and nothing is returned beyond acknowledgement. Clients call it best-effort as they close; a client that crashes simply never does, and the daemon then falls back to its idle period.

operations.summary: Move card to trash
operations.description: The card and every changed card are written in one commit. With children=promote (the default), the card's immediate live children take its place among its siblings (or the project's top level) in their existing order, keeping their own descendants; children already in Trash stay there. operations.name: get_events
operations.summary: Subscribe to committed daemon state changes (SSE)
operations.description:
Sends ready, then project.changed, card.changed, resource.changed,
location.changed, thread.changed, message.changed and run.changed invalidations.
Intermediate states can coalesce. Each frame has an opaque id and JSON data.
Without a cursor starts at the current tail. Last-Event-ID replays bounded
in-memory history. Restart, an expired cursor or last_revision without a
replayable cursor returns resync_required with current Git revisions and
history URLs, then closes. This endpoint does not synthesize events from Git.
Refresh current state on resync; Git is the durable project history.
Comments provide heartbeats. Disconnecting unsubscribes without cancelling jobs.
operations.response_description: Live SSE stream; ready or resync_required is the first event

parameters.name: last_revision
parameters.description: Last-known project Git revision for recovery; requires project_id. An unavailable replay explicitly requires refresh, even when HEAD is unchanged.

operations.name: post_projects_project_id_repair_hierarchy
operations.summary: Find, and optionally fix, cards hidden under missing or trashed parents
operations.description: A live card whose parent is missing or trashed cannot be reached by browsing from the project's top level. This can happen after an older client trashed a parent, a card file was removed by hand, or a sync brought either in. Without apply, this only reports, reading the database alone (so it works on a locked encrypted project). With apply, each hidden branch moves to its nearest live, reachable ancestor (or the top level), into the place its trashed ancestor held, with its descendants still attached, in one commit. Applying twice changes nothing the second time. Cards in parent cycles are reported and left alone. The daemon also repairs at startup and core repairs after every pull.
operations.response_description: The plan, and whether it was applied

errors.description: Invalid body, or a privacy error applying to an encrypted project

The keyring needed to write an encrypted project is unavailable

operations.name: get_projects_project_id_cards
operations.summary: Page through a project's live cards
operations.description: Filters combine. Each page reads current data; iteration is not a snapshot.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Exact tag match, case-insensitive, without the leading

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Omit for all hierarchy levels; roots selects root cards; a card ID selects its immediate children.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: updated_desc breaks ties by descending card ID. sort_key_asc follows sibling order and breaks ties by ascending card ID; use it with parent=roots or a parent card ID.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation from next_cursor. Keep the project, filters and ordering unchanged.

parameters.name: include_content
parameters.description: Include each card's body. The page is selected and every body read under one project lock, and the whole page fails if a body cannot be read (for example a locked encrypted project). limit is at most 1000 when true. The cursor is the same with or without content.

parameters.name: include_child_count
parameters.description: Include each returned live card's immediate live child count. The cursor is the same with or without counts.

operations.summary: Compare saved card versions or the change introduced by one revision
operations.description: In since mode, compares the explicitly selected from and to snapshots. In change mode, compares the first parent of to with to; a root commit is compared with a previously nonexistent card. Merge commits use only their first parent, not a combined multi-parent diff.

operations.name: post_projects_project_id_history_cards_card_id_restore
operations.summary: Restore a card to a saved snapshot
operations.description: Restores the complete card snapshot at the selected commit and records the result as a new commit without rewriting history. Lifecycle rules still apply. Restoring a snapshot in which the card was trashed promotes its current live children, as trashing does. Restoring a live snapshot places the card under a reachable parent, as restoring from Trash does.

parameters.name: oid
parameters.description: Revision containing the snapshot to restore.
